Half the time you left with something else entirely. A history of lighthouses or a book about how bridges are built, because it happened to sit on the shelf next to the one you wanted. That kind of accident is harder to come by now. Search is fast and precise, and it gives us exactly what we ask for, which means it rarely gives us what we didn't know to ask for. The second lesson was that patience is a skill, not a personality trait. The library allowed three books per visit, and interlibrary loans took two or three weeks to arrive. You learn to plan, to read slowly, and to finish what you started, because the next book was not going to appear the moment you got bored. I don't think we should go back to waiting weeks for a book, but I do think we lose something when nothing in our lives asks us to wait.
